mainTopic: Stories of hidden צדיקים whose prayers bring rain: אבא חלקיה and his wife, חנן הנחבא, רבי יונה, and the wonder-working words of רבי יצחק בן אלישיב.
overview: This amud continues a series of stories about hidden צדיקים whose prayers bring rain. It opens in the middle of the story of אבא חלקיה, a poor day laborer whom two חכמים were sent to ask for rain. The גמרא lists his odd behaviors. Then he and his wife pray quietly on the roof, and the clouds rise first from her corner. The חכמים ask about each odd action, and every one turns out to come from honesty, care with others' property, modesty, or wise use of what little he had. His wife's prayer was answered first because her צדקה helped the poor right away, or because she prayed for hooligans to repent rather than die. Next comes חנן הנחבא, who prayed for rain for the sake of children and hid from honor. רבי זריקא then contrasts the open, hopeful prayers of רב הונא and רב חסדא in בבל with the secret, certain prayers of רבי יונה in ארץ ישראל. Further stories show the power of רבי יונה's grave and of רבי יצחק בן אלישיב's words, which he later gave up. The amud ends as a new story begins: רבי יוסי בר אבין leaves his teacher to learn with רב אשי, and the reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: He ignores their greeting and carries his load strangely
steps.stepSummary: אבא חלקיה does not respond to the חכמים' greeting, and in the evening he carries the wood and hoe on one shoulder and his cloak on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not show them a friendly face. Toward evening, when he gathered firewood, he carried the wood and the hoe on one shoulder and his cloak on the other shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with the first strange things the חכמים noticed about אבא חלקיה. The גמרא is building a list of puzzles that will be explained later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not returning a greeting looks rude, especially toward חכמים. Putting the cloak on the shoulder instead of using it as padding under the wood also looks odd. Hold on to these details, because each one is explained later in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Showed a friendly face (returned a greeting)

phrases.english: And he did not show them a welcoming face.
phrases.notes: He did not return their greeting.

phrases.english: Toward evening, when he was gathering firewood,
he carried the wood and the hoe on one shoulder,
and the cloak on the other shoulder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun on the previous part of the daf, where the חכמים found אבא חלקיה working in the field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Description of אבא חלקיה's puzzling behavior: he ignores the greeting and carries wood and cloak on separate shoulders.

steps.title: Barefoot on the road, shoes in the water, clothes lifted in thorns
steps.stepSummary: He walks barefoot the whole way but puts on shoes when crossing water, and he lifts his clothing when passing through thorny bushes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole way he did not wear shoes, but when he reached water he put on his shoes. When he reached shrubs and thorns, he lifted up his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The story adds more strange behaviors to the list. These look backwards: shoes come off where they seem needed and go on where they seem useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally people wear shoes on the road and take them off in water. Normally people let their clothes protect their legs from thorns. אבא חלקיה does the opposite, setting up another puzzle for later.

phrases.english: The whole way he did not wear shoes,
but when he reached water, he put on his shoes.
When he reached shrubs and thorns,
he lifted up his clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of puzzling behaviors on the walk home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: More puzzling behavior: barefoot on land, shoes in water, clothes lifted in thorns.

steps.title: His wife greets him dressed up, and the order of entering the house
steps.stepSummary: When he reaches town, his wife comes out adorned to meet him. At the house, she enters first, then he, then the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the town, his wife came out to meet him, dressed in fine clothing. When he reached his house, his wife went in first, then he went in, and then the חכמים went in.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with what happened at the town and at his home. Two more puzzling details are added: his wife's dressing up, and the unusual order of entering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems strange for a pious man's wife to come out adorned in public. It also seems strange that the woman enters before the men and the guests. אבא חלקיה explains both later on this amud (steps 16 and 18).

phrases.english: When he reached the town,
his wife came out to meet him, adorned.
When he reached his house,
his wife entered first,
then he entered,
and then the Sages entered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story from the road into the town and home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His wife comes out adorned, and the entering order is wife, then him, then the guests.

steps.title: He eats without inviting them and gives the younger child more
steps.stepSummary: He eats bread without inviting the חכמים, and when dividing bread he gives the older child one piece and the younger child two.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sat and ate bread, and he did not say to the חכמים, 'Come, eat.' He divided bread among the children: to the older one he gave one piece, and to the younger one he gave two.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last item in the list of odd behaviors. It ends the description section before the story shifts to the prayer for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not inviting guests to eat looks like a lack of הכנסת אורחים. Giving more to the younger child also seems unfair. Like the other details, these are explained later.

keyTerms.meaning: Ate bread (literally, 'wrapped bread', meaning had a meal)
Come eat (an invitation to the meal)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has now listed all of אבא חלקיה's strange behaviors. Each one looks wrong at first, but the story will show that each came from careful honesty and good sense.

phrases.english: He sat and ate bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַר לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן תּוּ כְּרוּכוּ.
phrases.english: and did not say to the Sages: Come, eat.
He divided bread for the children:
to the older, one piece, and to the younger, two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues inside the house with the meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He does not invite the guests to eat, and he gives the younger child a double portion.

steps.title: He and his wife quietly pray on the roof, and clouds come from her side
steps.stepSummary: אבא חלקיה realizes why the חכמים came, and he and his wife pray on the roof secretly so they will not get credit. The clouds rise first from his wife's corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his wife: I know the חכמים came because of the rain. Let us go up to the roof and pray. Perhaps the הקדוש ברוך הוא will be appeased and rain will come, and we will not take credit for ourselves. They went up to the roof. He stood in one corner and she stood in another corner. Clouds first rose from the corner where his wife stood.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shifts from his odd behavior to the main event: the prayer for rain. He prays humbly and secretly with his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He wants the rain to come before anyone asks him, so it will not look like his merit. The detail that clouds came first from her corner shows that his wife's prayer was answered first. The reason for this is explained later in the story.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows the theme of the whole story: true צדיקים try to hide their greatness and avoid taking credit.

phrases.english: He said to his wife:

phrases.aramaic: יָדַעְנָא דְּרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם מִיטְרָא קָא אָתוּ,
phrases.english: I know that the Sages have come because of the rain.
Let us go up to the roof and pray for mercy.
Perhaps the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be appeased,
and rain will come,
and we will not take credit for ourselves.
They went up to the roof.
He stood in one corner,
and she stood in another corner.
The clouds rose first
from that corner of his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from describing his behavior to the prayer for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה and his wife pray secretly, and the clouds come first from her corner.

steps.title: He asks why they came and thanks ה׳ that they did not need him
steps.stepSummary: After coming down, he asks the חכמים why they came. They say they were sent to ask him to pray for rain, and he says 'Blessed is ה׳ who did not make you need אבא חלקיה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came down, he said to them: Why did the חכמים come? They said to him: The חכמים sent us to the Master, to pray for rain. He said to them: Blessed is the Omnipresent, Who did not make you need אבא חלקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה pretends he does not know why they came, and when they tell him, he points to the clouds as ה׳'s direct gift. He is hiding that his own prayer brought the rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He already knew why they came (see step 5), so his question is part of his humility. His blessing means: the rain is coming anyway, so you do not need me. He avoids any credit.

keyTerms.meaning: Master (a respectful way to address someone)

phrases.english: When he came down, he said to them:
Why have the Sages come?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: שַׁדַּרוּ לַן רַבָּנַן לְגַבֵּי דְּמָר
phrases.english: They said to him: The Sages sent us to the Master
to pray for mercy for rain.
He said to them: Blessed is the Omnipresent,
Who did not make you need Abba Ḥilkiyya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the prayer on the roof with his conversation with the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה humbly denies any role in bringing the rain.

steps.title: The Sages ask him to explain: why he did not return their greeting
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say they know the rain came because of him, and ask him to explain his puzzling actions, starting with why he ignored their greeting.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We know the rain came because of the Master. But let the Master tell us about these things that puzzle us: Why, when we greeted the Master, did the Master not show us a friendly face?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים see through his humility and now open a new section: a series of questions about each strange action from steps 1-4. This first question is about the greeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their words 'we know the rain came because of you' reject his attempt to hide his merit. Then they go back through the list in order, starting with the greeting from step 1.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: יָדְעִינַן דְּמִיטְרָא מֵחֲמַת מָר הוּא דַּאֲתָא,
phrases.english: We know that the rain came because of the Master,
but let the Master tell us
these things that are puzzling to us:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי יָהֵיבְנָא לְמָר שְׁלָמָא
phrases.english: What is the reason that when we greeted the Master,
the Master did not show us a welcoming face?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי יָהֵיבְנָא לְמָר שְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects his denial and opens the explanation section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he did not return their greeting.

steps.title: He was a hired worker and could not waste his employer's time
steps.stepSummary: He explains that he was hired for the day and did not want to stop working to answer them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I was a day laborer, and I said to myself: I will not stop working.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה answers the first question. His silence was not rudeness but honesty toward his employer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worker hired by the day owes his time to his employer. Stopping to chat would be like taking time that belongs to someone else. So what looked like disrespect was actually careful honesty.

keyTerms.meaning: Day laborer, worker hired for the day

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is often cited for the idea that a worker must not waste the time he is being paid for.

phrases.english: He said to them: I was a day laborer,
and I said: I will not stop working.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the greeting.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As a day laborer, his time belonged to his employer, so he could not stop to answer.

steps.title: Why the wood on one shoulder and the cloak on the other
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why he carried the wood on one shoulder and the cloak on the other instead of using the cloak as padding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason the Master carried the wood on one shoulder and the cloak on the other shoulder?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask about the second strange behavior, from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person would put the cloak under the wood to protect his shoulder. They want to know why he did not.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּרָא מָר צִיבֵי אַחַד כַּתְפֵּיהּ
phrases.english: And what is the reason the Master carried wood on one shoulder
and the cloak on the other shoulder?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא דְּרָא מָר צִיבֵי אַחַד כַּתְפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he did not place the cloak under the wood.

steps.title: The cloak was borrowed only for wearing
steps.stepSummary: He explains that the cloak was borrowed, and he had permission to wear it but not to carry wood on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It was a borrowed cloak. I borrowed it for this purpose (to wear), and I did not borrow it for that purpose (to put wood on it).
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה answers the second question. He was careful not to use a borrowed item beyond what the owner allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a borrowed object in a way the owner did not agree to is improper and could damage it. Wood would rub and tear the cloak. So he kept it separate, even though it hurt his own shoulder.

phrases.english: He said to them: It was a borrowed cloak.
For this I borrowed it, and for that I did not borrow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the cloak.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cloak was borrowed for wearing only, not for carrying wood.

steps.title: Why barefoot on the road but shoes in the water
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why he walked barefoot the whole way but put on shoes in the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the Master did not wear his shoes the whole way, but when he reached water he put on his shoes?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask about the third strange behavior, from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His shoe habits seem backwards, so they ask him to explain.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כּוּלַּהּ אוֹרְחָא לָא סָיֵים מָר מְסָאנֵיהּ
phrases.english: What is the reason the whole way the Master did not wear his shoes,
and when he reached water, he put on his shoes?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כּוּלַּהּ אוֹרְחָא לָא סָיֵים מָר מְסָאנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he wore shoes only in water.

steps.title: On the road he can see; in the water he cannot
steps.stepSummary: He explains that on the road he can see where he steps, but in water he cannot, so he needs shoes there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The whole way, I can see. In the water, I cannot see.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה answers the third question. He saved his shoes where he could protect his feet by looking, and wore them where he could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shoes were expensive, so he did not want to wear them out. On dry land he could watch for sharp things, but under water hidden dangers could hurt him. His behavior was practical, not strange.

phrases.english: He said to them: The whole way, I can see;
in the water, I cannot see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the shoes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He can watch his steps on land, but not in water, so shoes are needed only there.

steps.title: Why he lifted his clothes in the thorns
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why he lifted up his clothes when passing through shrubs and thorns.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that when the Master reached shrubs and thorns, he lifted up his clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask about the fourth strange behavior, also from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting clothes exposes the legs to scratches, which seems foolish. They want his reason.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
phrases.english: What is the reason that when the Master reached shrubs and thorns,
he lifted up his clothes?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he exposed his legs to the thorns.

steps.title: Skin heals, but torn clothing does not
steps.stepSummary: He explains that a scratch on his body will heal, but a tear in his clothing will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This (my skin) heals, and this (my garment) does not heal.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה answers the fourth question. He chose to risk his skin rather than his clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scratch on the body heals by itself, but a torn garment stays damaged and costs money to replace. For a poor man, protecting his clothes was the wiser choice. The explanations continue next.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, every strange action of אבא חלקיה turned out to have a good reason: honesty toward his employer, care with a borrowed item, and wise saving of his few possessions.

phrases.english: He said to them: This heals,
and this does not heal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the thorns.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Skin heals from scratches, but torn clothing does not.

steps.title: Why did your wife come out dressed up?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why אבא חלקיה's wife came out to meet him adorned when he got to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that when the Master reached the city, the Master's wife came out all dressed up?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים keep asking about the odd things they saw. Now they ask why his wife came out to meet him in fancy clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great צדיק's wife going out dressed up in public seems strange, even immodest. The חכמים want to know the hidden reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason
that when the Master reached the city
the Master's wife came out adorned?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי מְטָא מָר לְמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next question in the same series of questions to אבא חלקיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason his wife came out dressed up to greet him.

steps.title: So that I won't look at other women
steps.stepSummary: He explains that she dresses up so that his eyes stay on her and not on another woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: So that I will not set my eyes on another woman.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה answers that his wife dresses up for him. That way he will not look at other women while walking through the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What looked like a lack of modesty was really a way of guarding his eyes. His wife was helping him stay holy.

keyTerms.meaning: I will set my eyes (look at with desire)

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא אֶתֵּן עֵינַי בְּאִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: So that I will not set my eyes upon another woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא אֶתֵּן עֵינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She dresses up so that he will not look at other women.

steps.title: Why did she go in first, then you, then us?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask about the order in which everyone entered the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that she went in first, then the Master went in after her, and only then we went in?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask about the order of entering the house. The wife went first, then אבא חלקיה, and the guests went last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally guests are honored and allowed to go in first. Making them wait seemed rude, so they ask why.

phrases.english: What is the reason that she entered first,
and afterward the Master entered after her,
and only afterward we entered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the guests were made to enter last.

steps.title: Because I don't know you yet
steps.stepSummary: He explains he did not want unknown men alone with his wife, even for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Because I have not checked you out.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה answers that he does not know these guests well. So he made sure they would never be alone with his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the guests had gone in right behind his wife, they would have been alone with her for a moment. He kept himself between them to prevent that. It was caution, not disrespect.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא בְּדִיקִיתוּ לִי.
phrases.english: He said to them: Because you have not been checked by me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא בְּדִיקִיתוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did not yet trust the strangers to be alone with his wife.

steps.title: Why didn't you invite us to eat?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why he ate bread without inviting them to join.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that when the Master ate bread, he did not say to us: Come and eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask why אבא חלקיה ate his meal without inviting them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inviting guests to eat is basic הכנסת אורחים. Not even offering seemed very strange for a צדיק.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי כָּרֵיךְ מָר רִיפְתָּא
phrases.english: What is the reason that when the Master ate bread
he did not say to us: 'Come and eat'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי כָּרֵיךְ מָר רִיפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he did not invite them to eat.

steps.title: Not enough bread, so no fake invitation
steps.stepSummary: He explains he had too little bread, and did not want to get credit for an offer he could not really fulfill.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there was not much bread, and I said to myself: I should not get credit from the חכמים for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה explains there was only a little bread. Inviting them would have been an empty offer just to look generous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An invitation he knew they could not accept would earn him thanks he did not deserve. This is a form of גניבת דעת, misleading people, which he avoided.

phrases.english: Because there was not much bread,
and I said: I should not take from the Sages
credit for nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There was too little bread, and he would not make an empty offer to gain credit.

steps.title: Why more bread for the younger child?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why the older child got one piece of bread and the younger child got two.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the Master gave the older child one piece of bread and the younger one two?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask why he gave the younger child more bread than the older one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would expect an older child to need more food. The opposite seemed unfair or backwards.

phrases.english: What is the reason the Master gave
the older child one piece of bread
and the younger one two?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא יְהֵיב מָר לְיָנוֹקָא קַשִּׁישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the younger child got more bread.

steps.title: One stays home, the other learns in the בית כנסת
steps.stepSummary: He explains the older child is at home and can eat anytime, but the younger one sits learning all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This one stays at home, and this one sits in the בית כנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה explains that the older child is home and can grab food when hungry. The younger one sits learning in the בית כנסת and cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He divided food by real need, not by age. The child busy with תורה all day needs more when he eats.

phrases.english: He said to them: This one stays at home,
and this one sits in the synagogue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The older child can eat at home anytime; the younger one learns all day and needs more.

steps.title: Why did the clouds rise first on your wife's side?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask why the rain clouds first appeared from the corner where his wife was praying, before his own side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason the clouds rose first from that corner where the Master's wife was standing, before his own clouds?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last question. When they both prayed for rain, the clouds came first from his wife's corner, and the חכמים ask why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא חלקיה is the famous צדיק whom the חכמים came to for rain. So it is surprising that his wife's prayer was answered before his.

phrases.english: And what is the reason the clouds rose up first

phrases.aramaic: מֵהָךְ זָוִיתָא דַּהֲווֹת קָיְימָא דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּמָר
phrases.english: from that corner where the Master's wife was standing
before his own clouds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final question in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why his wife's prayer for rain was answered before his.

steps.title: Her charity helps the poor faster
steps.stepSummary: First answer: she gives bread, which helps the poor right away, while he gives money, which helps only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a woman is often at home, and she gives bread to the poor, so her benefit is immediate. But I give money, and my benefit is not immediate.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה gives his first explanation. His wife's צדקה reaches the poor faster than his, so her prayer was answered faster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread can be eaten right away. Money still has to be used to buy food, so it helps more slowly. Because her kindness is quicker, Heaven answered her more quickly, measure for measure.

phrases.english: Because a woman is often found at home,
and she gives bread to the poor,
so her benefit is immediate.
But I give money,
and its benefit is not immediate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her gift of bread helps the poor immediately; his gift of money helps only later.

steps.title: She prayed for the hooligans to repent
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: he prayed that the neighborhood hooligans should die, but she prayed that they repent, and they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: there were certain hooligans in our neighborhood. I prayed that they should die, and she prayed that they should repent. And they repented.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חלקיה gives a second, different reason. His wife's prayer about the hooligans was kinder and wiser than his, and it worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He prayed for the bad people to be gone, but she prayed for the badness to be gone. Her prayer was answered, which showed her greater standing in Heaven.
steps.whatToRemember: Every odd behavior of אבא חלקיה turned out to have a hidden, holy reason, and his wife was an equal partner in his righteousness.
steps.confusionAlert: Here תְּיוּבְתָּא means repentance, not the גמרא's usual technical 'refutation'.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: הָנְהוּ בִּירְיוֹנֵי דְּהָווּ בְּשִׁיבָבוּתַן,
phrases.english: Alternatively: those hooligans who were in our neighborhood,
I prayed that they should die,
and she prayed that they should return in repentance
[and they repented].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the same question as step 24; it ends the story of אבא חלקיה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She prayed for the hooligans to repent rather than die, and her prayer was answered.

steps.title: Children sent to חנן הנחבא for rain
steps.stepSummary: A new story: when rain was needed, the חכמים sent schoolchildren to חנן הנחבא, who grabbed his cloak and cried 'Father, give us rain!'
steps.simpleTranslation: חנן הנחבא was the son of the daughter of חוני המעגל. When the world needed rain, the חכמים would send schoolchildren to him. They grabbed the hem of his cloak and said to him: Father, Father, give us rain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about another grandson of חוני המעגל. This step sets the scene for his prayer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אבא חלקיה, he is a quiet צדיק from the family of חוני. The חכמים sent innocent children, whose plea would stir his prayer and Heaven's mercy.

phrases.english: Chanan HaNechba was the daughter's son
of Choni HaMe'aggel.
When the world needed rain,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ מְשַׁדְּרִי רַבָּנַן יָנוֹקֵי דְּבֵי רַב לְגַבֵּיהּ
phrases.english: the Sages would send schoolchildren to him
and they would grab him by the hem of his cloak,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אַבָּא, אַבָּא, הַב לַן מִיטְרָא!
phrases.english: and say to him: Father, Father, give us rain!

steps.triggerLanguage: חָנָן הַנֶּחְבָּא בַּר בְּרַתֵּיה דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about another descendant of חוני המעגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children were sent to חנן הנחבא to ask him for rain.

steps.title: Do it for the children who can't tell the difference
steps.stepSummary: חנן prays that ה׳ should bring rain for the sake of the children, who don't know the difference between their Father in Heaven and him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before the הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם! Act for the sake of these children, who cannot tell the difference between the Father Who gives rain and the father who does not give rain.
steps.whatsHappening: חנן turns the children's cry into a humble prayer. He asks ה׳ to answer for their sake, not his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children called him 'אבא', but he points out that only ה׳ is the true Father Who gives rain. He refuses to take credit and makes the children's innocence the reason for mercy.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the humility of this whole family of צדיקים: they bring rain but never claim the power as their own.

phrases.english: He said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! עֲשֵׂה בִּשְׁבִיל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: Master of the Universe! Act on behalf of these,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין בֵּין אַבָּא דְּיָהֵיב מִיטְרָא,
phrases.english: who cannot distinguish between the Father Who gives rain
and the father who does not give rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with חנן's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He asked for rain in the merit of the innocent children, giving all credit to ה׳.

steps.title: Why was he called 'the Hidden One'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he was called חנן הנחבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call him 'חנן הנחבא' (the Hidden One)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story to explain his nickname. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His name, 'the hidden one', seems to say something about who he was. The גמרא wants to know where it came from.

phrases.english: And why did they call him 'Chanan HaNechba'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the name given in step 26.

steps.title: He hid himself to avoid honor
steps.stepSummary: He was called 'the Hidden One' because he would hide himself in the lavatory so people would not honor him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would hide himself in the lavatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that he hid in the outhouse so people could not find him to honor him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He went to a place where no one would come looking, just to run away from honor. His name shows his deep humility, matching the humble prayer he said for the children.
steps.whatToRemember: חנן הנחבא, like אבא חלקיה, was a hidden צדיק: he brought rain yet ran away from honor and credit.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה מַחְבִּיא עַצְמוֹ בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא.
phrases.english: Because he would hide himself in the lavatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה מַחְבִּיא עַצְמוֹ בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He hid in the lavatory to escape honor.

steps.title: רבי זריקא sets up a comparison between ארץ ישראל and בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא tells רב ספרא to come and see the difference between the 'powerful ones' of ארץ ישראל and the 'pious ones' of בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said to רב ספרא: Come and see the difference between the powerful men of ארץ ישראל and the pious men of בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story with a setup line. רבי זריקא announces a comparison, and the next steps will fill in both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only introduces the two groups: תקיפי ארץ ישראל and חסידי בבל. The goal is to show how much greater the people of ארץ ישראל were, and the details come in the following steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'תקיפי' to mean bullies or strong-arm men. It means people whose prayers are spiritually powerful.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זְרִיקָא לְרַב סָפְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said to Rav Safra:
Come and see what the difference is between
the powerful men of Eretz Yisrael
and the pious men of Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story in the series about righteous people praying for rain, after the story of חנן הנחבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A comparison is announced between the חסידי בבל and the תקיפי ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The Babylonian approach: gather together and pray, hoping for rain
steps.stepSummary: The חסידי בבל, רב הונא and רב חסדא, would gather together when rain was needed and pray, saying perhaps הקב"ה would be appeased.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pious men of בבל are רב הונא and רב חסדא. When the world needed rain, they would say: Let us gather together and pray for mercy. Perhaps the הקדוש ברוך הוא will be appeased and bring rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the first side of the comparison: how the great people of בבל prayed for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their prayer was public, done as a group, and humble ('maybe ה׳ will answer'). The point of contrast is that the prayer was out in the open and the result was uncertain. The next step will show the opposite.

phrases.aramaic: חֲסִידֵי דְבָבֶל רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: The pious men of Babylonia are Rav Huna and Rav Chisda;
when the world was in need of rain
they would say: Let us gather together and pray for mercy;
perhaps the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be appeased
and bring rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲסִידֵי דְבָבֶל רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first side of the comparison announced in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חסידי בבל prayed for rain publicly and as a group, without being sure they would be answered.

steps.title: רבי יונה slips out with an excuse and prays alone in secret
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה, father of רבי מני, would tell his family he was going to buy grain. He then stood in a low, hidden place covered in sackcloth and prayed, and the rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: The powerful men of ארץ ישראל are like רבי יונה, the father of רבי מני. When the world needed rain, he would go into his house and say to his family: Give me my sack, and I will go buy a זוז's worth of grain. When he went outside, he would go and stand in a low place, as it is written: 'Out of the depths I have called You, ה׳.' He would stand in a hidden place, cover himself in sackcloth, and pray for mercy, and the rain would come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the second side of the comparison. רבי יונה prays for rain completely in secret, and his prayer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two contrasts with בבל. First, the prayer is private, with no gathering and even a cover story at home. Second, the result is certain: 'and the rain would come.' He stands in a low place because of the פסוק 'ממעמקים קראתיך,' which teaches that prayer should come from a place of lowliness.
steps.confusionAlert: The grain story is a cover so his family won't know he is going to pray. It is not the real reason he left the house.

phrases.english: The powerful men of Eretz Yisrael

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן רַבִּי יוֹנָה אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי מָנִי,
phrases.english: are like Rabbi Yona, the father of Rabbi Mani;
when the world was in need of rain,
he would enter his house and say to them (his family):
Give me my sack,
and I will go and bring myself a zuz's worth of grain.
When he went outside,
he would go and stand in a low place,
as it is written: 'Out of the depths I have called You, ה׳,'
and he would stand in a hidden place,
and cover himself with sackcloth, and pray for mercy,
and the rain would come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּקִּיפֵי דְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּגוֹן רַבִּי יוֹנָה אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי מָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting side to step 31: secret, solitary, and certain prayer versus public, communal, and hopeful prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יונה prayed for rain in total secrecy and humility, and he was answered.

steps.title: רבי יונה hides his miracle even from his family
steps.stepSummary: When he came home without grain, his family asked about it. He answered that since rain had come, prices would drop, so there was no need to buy now.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came home, they said to him: Did the Master bring grain? He said to them: I said to myself, since rain has come, now the world will have relief (and grain will become cheap).
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי יונה coming home empty-handed and giving his family a believable reason, so his prayer stays hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step completes the contrast. רבי יונה did not just pray privately. He made sure that even his own household never found out the rain came because of him, which is the height of humility.

keyTerms.meaning: Master (a respectful way of addressing someone)
The world will have relief (things will be plentiful)

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison teaches that the great people of ארץ ישראל prayed in total secrecy and were answered for sure. The חסידי בבל prayed openly and could only hope.

phrases.english: When he would come to his house,
they would say to him: Did the Master bring grain?
He said to them: I said (to myself),
since rain has come,
now the world will have relief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבי יונה story and shows the hiding was complete, even at home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יונה concealed his role in bringing the rain even from his own family.

steps.title: רבי מני's persecutors are stopped at his father's grave
steps.stepSummary: Members of the נשיא's household were harassing רבי מני. He cried out at his father's grave, and when they rode past, their horses' legs got stuck until they promised to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: members of the house of the נשיא were harassing רבי מני, his son. He threw himself down on his father's grave and said: Father, Father! These people are harassing me. One day they were passing there, and their horses' legs got stuck, until they took it upon themselves not to harass him anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word 'ותו' ('and furthermore'), the גמרא adds another story showing how powerful רבי יונה was, this time through his son רבי מני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the רבי יונה story. His spiritual power continued even after he died, protecting his son. The horses stayed stuck until the harassers committed to stop, which made it clear the miracle came for that reason.

phrases.english: And furthermore: Rabbi Mani, his son,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ קָא מְצַעֲרִי לֵיהּ דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה.
phrases.english: members of the house of the Nasi were harassing him.
He prostrated himself on his father's grave

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַבָּא אַבָּא! הָנֵי מְצַעֲרוּ לִי.
phrases.english: and said to him: Father, Father! These people are harassing me.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲווֹ קָא חָלְפִי הָתָם,
phrases.english: One day they were passing by there;
the legs of their horses got stuck
until they took upon themselves
that they would not harass him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further example of רבי יונה's greatness, shown through his son after his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יונה's merit protected his son from persecution even after his death.

steps.title: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב says the rich in-laws should become poor, and they do
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני complained to his teacher רבי יצחק בן אלישיב that his wealthy in-laws were harassing him. רבי יצחק said they should become poor, and they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבי מני was often found before רבי יצחק בן אלישיב. He said to him: The rich people of my father-in-law's house are harassing me. He said: Let them become poor. And they became poor.
steps.whatsHappening: Another 'ותו' story about רבי מני. This time a great teacher's words are fulfilled immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that the words of a צדיק like רבי יצחק בן אלישיב come true right away. The in-laws harassed רבי מני because of their wealth, so taking away the wealth was meant to solve the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Was often found before him (a regular student)

phrases.english: And furthermore: Rabbi Mani was often found
before Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elyashiv.
He said to him: The wealthy people of my father-in-law's house
are harassing me.
He said: Let them become poor. And they became poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: רַבִּי מָנִי הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about רבי מני, now showing the power of his teacher's words rather than his father's merit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב's statement that the harassers should become poor was immediately fulfilled.

steps.title: Now poor, they pressure him for money, so they become rich again
steps.stepSummary: Once poor, the in-laws pressured רבי מני for support. רבי יצחק said they should become rich again, and they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: They are pressuring me (for money). He said: Let them become rich. And they became rich.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a twist. Poverty caused a new problem, so רבי יצחק reversed it, and that was also fulfilled at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making them poor did not help, because now they leaned on רבי מני for money. The reversal shows that רבי יצחק's words worked in both directions.
steps.whatToRemember: These closing stories show the spiritual power of רבי יונה's family and circle: רבי יונה's grave protected his son רבי מני, and the words of רבי מני's teacher, רבי יצחק בן אלישיב, came true immediately.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Mani) said: They are pressuring me.
He (Rabbi Yitzchak) said: Let them become rich. And they became rich.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and resolves step 35. The first solution created a new problem, which is now reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב reversed his words and the in-laws became rich again, showing his words were fulfilled either way.

steps.title: רבי יצחק makes חנה beautiful
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני complains that his wife is not pleasing to him. רבי יצחק בן אלישיב asks her name and declares that חנה should become beautiful, and she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: My wife is not pleasing to me. רבי יצחק asked: What is her name? He answered: חנה. רבי יצחק said: Let חנה become beautiful. And she became beautiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי מני brings another personal problem to his teacher רבי יצחק בן אלישיב, and his teacher's words change reality again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third complaint רבי מני brings to רבי יצחק, after the two about his in-laws. The pattern stays the same: a short declaration from רבי יצחק immediately comes true. Asking for her name fits the idea that a blessing is directed at a specific, named person.

keyTerms.meaning: Are not pleasing / acceptable to me
Members of my household, meaning my wife

steps.confusionAlert: "אִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתִי" literally means "the people of my house," but here it means his wife. This is a common polite way to refer to one's wife.

phrases.english: He said: They are not pleasing to me
phrases.notes: רבי מני is speaking to רבי יצחק בן אלישיב.

phrases.english: the members of my household
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying "my wife."

phrases.english: He said to him: What is her name? Chana.
Let Chana become beautiful. And she became beautiful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: לָא מִיקַּבְּלִי עֲלַי אִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another complaint from רבי מני to the same teacher, continuing the series in steps 35-36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב's word made רבי מני's wife beautiful.

steps.title: חנה becomes haughty and is returned to her old appearance
steps.stepSummary: After becoming beautiful, חנה acts haughtily toward רבי מני. רבי יצחק declares that she should return to her former plain appearance, and she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said to him: She acts haughtily toward me. רבי יצחק said: If so, let חנה return to her plain appearance. And חנה returned to her plain appearance.
steps.whatsHappening: The solution causes a new problem, so רבי יצחק undoes his blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the pattern of the in-laws story. They became poor, then rich again. Here, חנה became beautiful and then plain again. Each change solved one problem but created another, so the original situation was restored.

keyTerms.meaning: She acts haughtily / shows off toward me
Her blackness, meaning her former plain appearance

steps.whatToRemember: Every "fix" רבי יצחק makes for רבי מני ends up being reversed. This prepares the next story, where רבי יצחק says he gave up this kind of power.

phrases.english: He said to him: She acts haughtily toward me.
He said to him: If so
let Chana return to her plain appearance,
phrases.notes: Literally "her blackness," meaning her former, less attractive look.

phrases.english: and Chana returned to her plain appearance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the blessing given in step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessing was undone, and חנה returned to her original appearance.

steps.title: רבי יצחק says he sent away his power
steps.stepSummary: Two students ask רבי יצחק בן אלישיב to pray that they become very wise. He answers that he once had that power but sent it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two students who learned before רבי יצחק בן אלישיב said to him: Let the master pray for us that we become very wise. He said to them: It was with me, and I sent it away.
steps.whatsHappening: A new short story about the same רבי יצחק. This time he refuses a request, explaining that he gave up his power to change things through prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the earlier stories, we would expect him to grant the students' request. Instead, he reveals that he deliberately let go of this ability. That fits the lesson of the previous stories, where changing reality kept backfiring.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master pray for mercy
That we should become very wise
It was with me, and I sent it away

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the series of stories. Even a great צדיק whose prayers are answered may choose not to use that power to change the natural order.

phrases.english: There were these two students

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲווֹ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁיב,
phrases.english: who were learning before Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elyashiv,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: נִיבְעֵי מָר רַחֲמֵי עֲלַן
phrases.english: They said to him: Let the master pray for mercy for us
that we should become very wise.
He said to them: It was with me, and I sent it away.
phrases.notes: "It" refers to the power to change things through prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ תְּרֵי תַלְמִידֵי דַּהֲווֹ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְיָשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of stories about רבי יצחק בן אלישיב by showing he gave up his wonder-working power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן אלישיב gave up his ability to change reality through prayer.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר אבין leaves his teacher for רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין regularly learned before רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת, but he left him and went to learn before רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין was often found learning before רבי יוסי from יוקרת. He left him and came to learn before רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story here. This line only sets the scene: a student left his teacher. The explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new story begins with a hint of a problem, since a regular student abandoned his teacher. The reader is meant to wonder why he left, and the story continues on the next amud to answer that.

keyTerms.meaning: He was regularly found before him, meaning he studied with him often

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin was frequently found
before Rabbi Yosei from Yokrat.
He left him, and came to learn before Rav Ashi.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמִן יוֹקֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, moving on from רבי יצחק בן אלישיב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: רבי יוסי בר אבין left רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת to learn with רב אשי.
